newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude has $19.28 Fibonacci support.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude has $19.28 Fibonacci support.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
----------------- VIEWS FROM THE MARKET - July 8 --------------
+ NYMEX crude futures are still looking bearish on Tuesday but traders expect to find Fibonacci support at $19.28.
+ Daily stochastics are overbought and this is a further signal that prices may test downwards.
NYMEX crude futures are looking bearish although support at $19.28 is expected to provide an obstacle for any strong downwards move, technical analysts said.
NYMEX crude oil closed four cents a barrel down at $19.52 on Monday and heating oil was just 0.02 cent a gallon firmer at 52.78. August gasoline also gained just 0.02 cent to close at 57.94.

Tom Bentz at High Yield Analytics in New York said that while some of the short-term signals were conflicting, there was still room for more downwards movement, but that the market was likely to rally in the much longer term.

He said August crude's failure on Monday to break clearly below $19.28, the 61.8 percent Fibonacci retracement of the upwards move from the $18.65 low on June 20 to the $20.39 high on July 2, was supportive, and this number would again form an obstacle to further falls.
But he said Thursday's downwards move had convincingly pierced an important supportive trendline and this was a bearish signal.
And he added: "The daily stochastics are in overbought territory and we may have a bit more work to do on the downside."
This, he said, could lead to a test of $19.00 - not only an important psychological number but also an area of previous congestion.
Below this level lies the August chart contract low at $18.65 and the continuation chart low of $18.35 on June 20.
He said that in the longer term, however, the market was likely to rally. "That is the way I am leaning."
He said weekly stochastics had created a bullish divergence pattern, where the weekly prices make new lows but the momentum indicators do not.
Fenella Graham at MeesPierson Derivatives in London, employing the Market Profile chart technique, also pegged support at $19.28, then $19.00.
She said in a daily report she saw resistance for gasoline at 58.20 cents a gallon. "We look to add to shorts at this level again and join any breaks lower.
"A break above 58.20, or a buying extreme, and we cut any shorts, otherwise profit-taking waits until 56.70.
-- Nicholas Shaxson, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8167
